data_quality_concerns: Unit inconsistency: milestone is nominally 'Steam 1M+ sold' but the cohort mixes copies-sold with 'players reached'. F2P titles (Marvel Rivals, NARAKA, Zenless, Wuthering Waves, Delta Force, Fall Guys) and Game Pass titles (Starfield, Sea of Thieves, Forza Horizon 5, Indiana Jones, Oblivion Remastered, Grounded) hit 1M via cross-platform/free players, not Steam units. inflation_flag on 54% (60/111) confirms this is systemic.
F2P selection is arbitrary: some F2P/gacha titles are in, but far larger ones (Apex Legends, Counter-Strike 2, Warzone, Genshin, Once Human, Rocket League) are excluded with no stated rule.
96% self-reported milestones (107/111) with almost no third-party (VG Insights) corroboration; publisher press-release numbers are systematically upward-biased.

coder_disagreement_pct_AB = 45% on the CENTRAL fit classification. Nearly half the fit calls are coin-flips, so the flagship '55% fit' headline has an error band (~40-70%) wide enough to be non-informative; every downstream fit-rate split inherits this instability.

Window contradiction: stated window is 2020-2026 but games_by_year includes 2011, 2013, 2016 (x5), 2018, 2019 (GTA V, Terraria, Factorio, Grim Dawn, Astroneer, Dead Cells, Hunt: Showdown). The inclusion rule (release-date vs sold-in-window) is never fixed, so legacy long-tail sellers are silently mixed with new releases.

Small, salience-selected sample: true Steam 1M+ population 2020-2026 is many hundreds; 125 hand-picked candidates skewed toward discourse-heavy/viral titles is a survivorship + recall bias that inflates the 'interesting' rates (co-op, streamer, twist-fit).
Multi-label tables (twist_type_freq sums to ~247, base/non-fit) have no disclosed per-title cap; overlapping percentages can double-count and are not mutually exclusive.
Recency truncation: 2025 (17) and 2026 (4) are undercounted vs 2024 (31) simply because recent titles haven't accrued/reported 1M yet, biasing time-trend claims (e.g. the '2023 AAA-sequel' dip).
licensed_IP fits at 0% is partly circular — 'twist' was defined in a way that structurally excludes brand-driven AAA, so the counterexample finding is baked into the coding scheme.
missing_famous_titles: Lethal Company (2023) — the single most glaring omission; ~10M+ Steam, the definitional co-op 'friendslop' hit that anchors their entire virality/co-op thesis
Street Fighter 6 (2023) — 1M+; whole fighting-game genre underrepresented
Total War: Warhammer III (2022) — 1M+; strategy/4X near-absent
Crusader Kings III (2020), Age of Empires IV (2021), Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020) — major grand-strategy/sim 1M+ sellers, category is a blind spot
Football Manager 24 (and prior annual entries) — 1M+ each

Sony PC ports: God of War (2022), Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered (2022), The Last of Us Part I (2023), Horizon Forbidden West (2024), God of War Ragnarok (2024), Marvel's Spider-Man 2 (2025) — an entire premium single-player brand-driven category missing
ARK: Survival Ascended (2023), Raft (2022), 7 Days to Die 1.0 (2024) — major survival 1M+ omissions
Supermarket Simulator (2024) — viral 1M+ sim, fits their cheap-sim tier
Final Fantasy VII Rebirth (2025 PC) and Final Fantasy XVI (2024 PC) — AAA JRPG 1M+ sellers
over_or_under_counted_dimensions: coop_social OVER-counted: 66.7% co-op is inflated by deliberate inclusion of the viral co-op cluster (PEAK, Content Warning, R.E.P.O., Chained Together, Liar's Bar, Human: Fall Flat, Goose Goose Duck) while premium single-player 1M+ titles (esp. missing Sony ports) are under-sampled. True population co-op share is far lower.
virality_streamer OVER-counted for the same salience reason — 68% streamer / 61% short-form is a property of how titles were selected, not of Steam 1M+ sellers at large.

genre_distribution: strategy/4X/grand-strategy and management-sim are severely UNDER-counted (missing CK3, AoE4, TWW3, Football Manager, MSFS, Two Point). Action-RPG's 23% 'largest genre' claim is partly an artifact of these gaps.
Fighting games UNDER-counted (missing SF6, Tekken 8, Guilty Gear); genre effectively absent.

Premium single-player / AAA-brand UNDER-counted (Sony ports, FF XVI/Rebirth). Adding them would push fits_pct_AB DOWN and undercut the 55% headline — the sample is biased toward the exact viral-indie tier the hypothesis explains.

region: Europe 46% and especially Sweden 13% likely OVERSTATED by selection toward Coffee Stain/Landfall-type viral indies; Japanese, Korean and Chinese output is under-sampled given missing JP/CN titles.
solo_or_tiny_pct and team_size medians are biased LOW by the same indie-viral oversampling; the 'small teams fit 86%' correlation is partly a sampling artifact.
survival-crafting is prominent but still missing its biggest 2022-2024 entries (ARK Ascended, Raft, 7DTD), so intra-genre counts are unreliable.
Year counts: 2025-2026 UNDER-counted due to recency truncation, distorting the time-trend narrative.
critic.overall_assessment: The 125-title set is a curated, salience-biased convenience sample rather than a representative census of Steam 1M+ sellers 2020-2026, and that biases the study toward confirming its own hypothesis. It over-samples the viral co-op indie tier the 'familiar base + novel twist' pattern explains, while systematically omitting whole brand/AAA categories that would read as fits=false: Sony single-player PC ports (God of War, Spider-Man, TLOU), strategy/4X (CK3, AoE4, Total War: Warhammer III, Football Manager), fighting games (SF6, Tekken 8), and — most damningly — Lethal Company, the archetypal co-op hit their thesis is built around. Adding the missing AAA/brand titles would push the 55% fit figure down; the sample's composition is doing analytical work. Compounding this, 96% of milestones are self-reported, 54% carry inflation flags, the copies-sold vs players-reached unit is inconsistent (F2P and Game Pass titles counted as 'sales'), F2P inclusion is arbitrary, and the 2020-2026 window is violated by 2011-2019 legacy titles. Most critically, 45% coder disagreement on the central fit label means the headline 'roughly half fit' is statistically soft — its true value could plausibly sit anywhere from ~40% to ~70%. Treat all fit-rate splits as directional at best, not quantitative."

redteam_ko:
생존자 편향이 이 연구의 치명적 결함이다. 표본은 100만 장 이상 팔린 히트작 125개뿐이고, "친숙한 기반 + 참신한 비틀기"를 시도했다가 실패한 수천 개의 게임(대조군)이 전혀 없기 때문에, 이 데이터는 "히트작 중 약 절반이 이 패턴을 보인다"까지만 말할 수 있을 뿐 "이 패턴이 히트 확률을 높인다"는 인과·예측적 주장은 원리적으로 증명할 수 없다 — 같은 공식을 따른 실패작이 히트작보다 훨씬 많을 수도 있다.

둘째, 55%라는 수치 자체가 단일 분석가의 주관적 코딩(base_familiarity, twist novelty, 그리고 "브랜드/제작비가 진짜 동인"이라는 판단성 강등)에 전적으로 의존하며, 저자 스스로 순수 공식 기준으로는 64%까지 튄다고 인정한다. 즉 헤드라인 숫자는 임계값과 판정 기준을 어디에 긋느냐에 따라 54~64%를 오가는데, 이는 발견이 아니라 코딩 재량의 산물이다. 게다가 정의가 극도로 탄력적이어서 — 포커, 러시안 룰렛, 청소, 농사, 포켓몬 등 거의 모든 것을 사후적으로 "친숙한 기반 + 비틀기"로 서술할 수 있으므로, 이 프레임은 반증 불가능에 가깝고 설명력이 낮다(실제로 45%는 이 틀에 맞지도 않았다).

셋째, 히트의 실제 동인은 이 패턴 자체가 아니라 더 값싸고 흔한 교란변수 — 협동 플레이(66.7%), 스트리머·숏폼 바이럴(67.6%/61.3%), 낮은 가격(중앙값 $39.99, 31.5%가 $20 미만), 코로나·장르 공백 같은 타이밍 — 와 강하게 얽혀 있는데, 이 요인들이 "비틀기"와 분리되어 통제되지 않았기 때문에 성공을 비틀기 덕으로 귀속시킬 근거가 없다. 결론적으로 이 데이터가 증명할 수 있는 것은 "최근 히트작의 절반가량이 사후적으로 이 패턴으로 서술 가능하다"는 서술적 사실뿐이며, "이 패턴을 따르라"는 처방적·전략적 조언의 근거로는 쓸 수 없다.
